curatorBrief.title: Welcome to the Short 'a' Word Workshop!
curatorBrief.intent: Welcome Kindergarten learners with an engaging, audio-rich hook about the short 'a' sound (/ă/ as in apple and cat). Introduce our three missions: hearing the short 'a' sound, blending letter sounds into 3-letter CVC words, and reading words all the way through to solve word puzzles.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Listen to and identify the short 'a' sound in spoken words.

components.title: Meet the Short 'a' Sound
components.intent: Introduce the short 'a' sound (/ă/) with vibrant, friendly visual anchor cards such as an apple, an alligator, an ant, and an astronaut to build phonemic awareness without requiring reading.

components.title: Say the Short 'a' Sound
components.intent: Guide learners through live direct-instruction phonemic practice to isolate, stretch, and speak the continuous short vowel sound /ă/, reinforcing grapheme-phoneme connection with live tutor audio feedback.

components.title: Sound Detective: Finding /ă/
components.intent: Provide spoken phonemic awareness challenges where students listen to spoken words and identify words that have the short 'a' sound, utilizing supportive picture cues.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Connect letter sounds to written letters to decode simple CVC words.

components.title: Blend Sounds Together
components.intent: Model continuous sound-by-sound blending for short 'a' CVC words (like c-a-t, b-a-t, m-a-p) using Elkonin-style phoneme tiles and audio playback that blend into whole words.

components.title: Build and Spell Short 'a' Words
components.intent: Guide students to map spoken sounds to letters by placing consonant-vowel-consonant tiles into boxes to spell target short 'a' words with live tutor support.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Read a short CVC word all the way through to discover the secret word.

components.title: Read the Mystery Word
components.intent: Direct instruction reading drill where the child sees printed short 'a' CVC words (e.g., cat, jam, pan, fan) and reads them aloud into the microphone to reveal the secret meaning.

components.title: Secret Word Match
components.intent: Challenge students to decode printed short 'a' CVC words and match them with the corresponding picture or distinguish real words from silly nonsense words, proving full decoding mastery.

finalAssessment.title: Short 'a' Word Master Badge
finalAssessment.intent: Assess all three objectives: recognizing the short 'a' sound in spoken words, identifying the correct letter sounds to form a CVC word, and matching decoded short 'a' words with their corresponding pictures.

problems.question: Which word has the short a sound?
problems.rationale: The word cat has the short a sound in the middle, making the /æ/ sound like in apple. When we blend the sounds /k/, /æ/, and /t/, we make the word cat. The words dog and sun have different vowel sounds.
problems.teachingNote: Encourage learners to segment each word by tapping their fingers or stretching their arms for each phoneme (/k/ - /æ/ - /t/) to help isolate the medial vowel sound.
successCriteria: Identify the short a vowel sound in a CVC word.
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.statement: The letter a in the word cat makes the short a sound.
problems.rationale: The word cat is a simple CVC word where the letter a sits in the middle and makes the short a sound, just like in hat and bat. When sounding out c-a-t, we blend the short a sound between the consonant sounds.
problems.teachingNote: Help students practice touching each letter and making the sound before blending them together to hear the whole word.
successCriteria: Identify the short a sound in CVC words
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word finishes the sentence: Pat wore a h_t?
problems.rationale: Adding the short a sound to the middle of 'h_t' spells the word 'hat' (/h/ /æ/ /t/). Pat can wear a hat on his head. 'Bat' and 'cap' do not have the same starting or ending sounds as 'h_t'.
problems.teachingNote: Guide students to isolate the beginning sound /h/ and ending sound /t/, then blend them with the short a sound /æ/ to decode 'hat'.
successCriteria: Decode a CVC word with the short a vowel sound.
Identify the correct CVC word that completes a sentence.
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: What animal do the sounds /k/ /a/ /t/ make?
problems.rationale: When we blend the sounds /k/, /a/, and /t/ together, they make the word 'cat.' A bat begins with the /b/ sound, and a rat begins with the /r/ sound.
problems.teachingNote: Encourage students to use continuous blending by stretching each sound smoothly without pausing before saying the full word quickly.
successCriteria: Blend individual phonemes in a short a CVC word to identify the spoken word.
Distinguish between CVC words that share the -at word family ending based on the initial sound.
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word has the short a sound?
problems.rationale: When we stretch out the sounds in cat, we hear /k/, /æ/, and /t/. The middle sound is the short a sound, just like in bat and map. Dog has a short o sound and pig has a short i sound.
problems.teachingNote: Have students place a hand on their chin or tap their fingers to isolate the middle vowel sound when blending CVC words.
successCriteria: Identify the short a vowel sound in a CVC word
Distinguish the short a vowel sound from other short vowel sounds
